concepts.def: Emile Durkheim's Elementary Forms 1912: 'unified system of beliefs and practices relative to sacred things'; functionalist sociological approach.
Judaism, Christianity, Islam; trace descent from Abraham; monotheistic; share Hebrew Bible/Torah and ethical monotheism.
Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, Sikhism originating in Indian subcontinent; share karma, dharma and rebirth concepts.
Chinese family including Daoism, Confucianism and folk religion; emphasise harmony, yin-yang and ancestor veneration.
Ninian Smart's Seven Dimensions of Religion 1989: doctrinal, mythical, ethical, ritual, experiential, social, material.
Friedrich Max Muller's 1870 founding of comparative religion at Royal Institution; 'he who knows one knows none'.

concepts.def: Earliest scriptures (Rig, Sama, Yajur, Atharva); composed c.1500-500 BCE in Vedic Sanskrit; foundation of shruti.
Late Vedic philosophical texts c.800-200 BCE; explore Brahman-Atman identity; Mundaka, Katha, Brihadaranyaka principal ones.
Brahma (creator), Vishnu (preserver), Shiva (destroyer); structural divine triad in puranic Hinduism.
Karma is action and consequence; samsara the cycle of rebirth; moksha is liberation from samsara.
700-verse dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna c.400 BCE - 200 CE within Mahabharata; teaches three yogas — karma, bhakti, jnana.
Four social orders (brahmin, kshatriya, vaishya, shudra) and four life stages (brahmacharya, grihastha, vanaprastha, sannyasa).

concepts.def: Born Lumbini c.480 BCE; renounced palace life at 29; achieved enlightenment under Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya.
Dukkha (suffering), samudaya (cause is craving), nirodha (cessation), magga (Eightfold Path); first sermon at Sarnath.
Right view, intention, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, concentration; grouped into wisdom, ethics, meditation.
Anicca (impermanence), dukkha (suffering), anatta (non-self); shared across Theravada and Mahayana traditions.
Theravada uses Pali canon (Tipitaka) and arahant ideal; Mahayana adds Sanskrit sutras and bodhisattva path for all beings.
Tantric Buddhism dominant in Tibet, Bhutan, Mongolia; mantra, mudra and mandala practice; Dalai Lama Gelug tradition.

concepts.def: Founder born at Talwandi (now Nankana Sahib); proclaimed Ik Onkar (one God) after immersion at Sultanpur 1499.
Lineage from Nanak to Guru Gobind Singh; Guru Granth Sahib installed as eternal Guru in 1708 at Nanded.
Sikh scripture compiled by Guru Arjan 1604; expanded by Guru Gobind Singh; 1,430 angs and 31 ragas of devotional poetry.
Founded by Guru Gobind Singh at Anandpur Sahib Vaisakhi day; Panj Pyare (Five Beloved Ones) initiated through amrit.
Kesh (uncut hair), Kangha (comb), Kara (steel bracelet), Kachera (cotton breeches), Kirpan (sword); Khalsa identity markers.
Naam Japna (meditate on Name), Kirat Karna (honest work), Vand Chakna (share with others); foundational Sikh ethics.

concepts.def: Five Books of Moses (Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy); part of Tanakh with Nevi'im and Ketuvim.
Berit between God and Israel; Abrahamic c.1800 BCE, Mosaic at Sinai c.1300 BCE, Davidic and New Covenants in prophets.
Commandments enumerated by Maimonides c.1170 CE; includes 248 positive and 365 negative commandments.
Mishnah (c.200 CE Judah ha-Nasi) plus Gemara; Babylonian Talmud completed c.500 CE; oral Torah commentary.
Orthodox, Conservative (Solomon Schechter, US), Reform (1810 Germany under Israel Jacobson), Reconstructionist (Mordecai Kaplan 1934).

concepts.def: Doctrine of Christ's nature; Council of Chalcedon 451 CE affirmed two natures (divine and human) in one person.
Doctrine of one God in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit); Council of Nicaea 325 CE defined homoousios.
Catholic, Orthodox (Great Schism 1054), Protestant (Luther's 95 Theses 1517); Oriental Orthodox after Chalcedon.
Catholic seven (baptism, confirmation, eucharist, reconciliation, anointing, marriage, holy orders); Protestant two (baptism, eucharist).
Lutheran principle of scripture alone as authority; with sola fide and sola gratia constitute three solas of Reformation.
1962-65 under John XXIII and Paul VI; renewed Catholic liturgy (vernacular Mass), ecumenism (Unitatis Redintegratio) and religious freedom.

concepts.def: Sacred text revealed to Muhammad 610-632 CE; 114 surahs; compiled under Caliph Uthman c.650 CE; recited in classical Arabic.
Shahada (creed), Salah (five daily prayers), Zakat (alms), Sawm (Ramadan fasting), Hajj (pilgrimage to Mecca).
Reports of Muhammad's sayings and actions; Sunni canonical six books include Sahih al-Bukhari c.846 and Sahih Muslim c.875.
Islamic law derived from Quran, Sunnah, ijma (consensus), qiyas (analogy); four Sunni schools — Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali.
Originated in succession dispute after Muhammad's death 632 CE; Battle of Karbala 680 CE pivotal; Shia number ~15% globally.
Mystical Islam emphasising tariqa and dhikr; Al-Ghazali c.1100 reconciled with orthodoxy; Rumi (d.1273) founded Mevlevi order.

concepts.def: Traditionally attributed to Laozi 6th century BCE; 81-chapter text on the Dao, wu wei and ziran.
4th century BCE philosopher; Inner Chapters include butterfly dream and cook Ding parables; celebrates spontaneity.
The Way underlying reality; ineffable, source of yin and yang; cannot be named permanently per Daodejing 1.
Non-coercive action in alignment with Dao; not passivity but effortless responsiveness; key political principle of early Han.
Celestial Masters founded by Zhang Daoling 142 CE; rituals, alchemy, immortality cults; Quanzhen and Zhengyi major sects.
Complementary cosmic principles paired with five phases (wood, fire, earth, metal, water); cyclic generation and destruction.

concepts.def: Born 551 BCE in Lu state; itinerant teacher; Analects (Lunyu) compiled by disciples after his death 479 BCE.
Humaneness or benevolence; core Confucian virtue; expressed through reciprocity (shu) and adherence to ritual.
Ritual propriety; correct conduct in family, social and political relations; basis for moral cultivation in the Liji.
Mencius (372-289 BCE) argued human nature is good; Xunzi (310-235 BCE) argued it is bad and requires ritual correction.
Yijing (Changes), Shujing (Documents), Shijing (Odes), Liji (Rites), Chunqiu (Spring and Autumn); imperial canon.
Song dynasty revival; Zhu Xi (1130-1200) systematised orthodoxy through Four Books (Analects, Mencius, Great Learning, Doctrine of the Mean).

concepts.def: Persian noble Mirza Husayn-Ali Nuri; proclaimed mission 1863 in Baghdad Garden of Ridvan; exiled to Akka 1868.
Siyyid Ali-Muhammad Shirazi declared in 1844 he was the Bab (gate) and herald; executed in Tabriz 1850.
Manifestations of God appear in successive ages (Krishna, Buddha, Christ, Muhammad, Bahaullah); each renews eternal religion.
Baha'i Most Holy Book; lays out laws, marriage, prayer (Nineteen-Day Feast) and inheritance; written in Arabic in Akka.
Supreme elected governing body in Haifa since 1963; nine members re-elected every five years.
Oneness of God, oneness of religion, oneness of humanity; equality of women and men; harmony of science and religion.

John Hick's God Has Many Names 1980 pluralism contrasts with exclusivism (one true religion) and inclusivism (one privileged path).
Christian salvation by grace, Islamic submission, Buddhist enlightenment, Hindu moksha; varied teleologies.
Victor Turner's liminality 1969 (drawn from Van Gennep 1909) analyses rites of passage across traditions.
Karl Jaspers's Vom Ursprung und Ziel der Geschichte 1949 dated transformation 800-200 BCE across Greece, India, China, Iran, Israel.

concepts.def: Das Heilige 1917 describes mysterium tremendum et fascinans; non-rational core of religion.
Varieties of Religious Experience 1902 Gifford Lectures; four marks of mystical experience: ineffability, noetic quality, transiency, passivity.
Negative theology of Pseudo-Dionysius c.500 CE and Meister Eckhart (d.1328); knows God by what God is not.
Rabia of Basra (d.801) introduced divine love; al-Hallaj (executed 922) declared 'Ana al-Haqq'; Rumi (d.1273) and Ibn Arabi (d.1240).
Teresa of Avila (d.1582) Interior Castle, John of the Cross (d.1591) Dark Night, Julian of Norwich (d.c.1416) Revelations.
Advaita non-dualism of Shankara (788-820); identifies Atman with Brahman; samadhi as direct realisation.

concepts.def: Morality grounded in God's commands; Plato's Euthyphro 399 BCE poses dilemma: is the pious loved because pious, or pious because loved?
Thomas Aquinas's Summa Theologiae I-II q.94 (1265-74); eternal law accessible through reason; primary precepts of preservation, procreation, society.
Five Precepts: refrain from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, false speech, intoxicants; complements Eightfold Path.
Cultivation of ren (humaneness), yi (righteousness), li (propriety), zhi (wisdom), xin (trustworthiness); five constant virtues.
Gustavo Gutierrez's A Theology of Liberation 1971; preferential option for the poor; influenced Brazilian CEBs and Oscar Romero.

concepts.def: Aquinas's Five Ways (1265-74) include first cause and contingency arguments; revived by William Lane Craig as Kalam version.
Anselm's Proslogion 1078 defines God as 'that than which nothing greater can be conceived'; revised by Descartes and Plantinga.
William Paley's Natural Theology 1802 watchmaker analogy; revived by Intelligent Design and fine-tuning arguments.
A J Ayer's Language, Truth and Logic 1936 dismissed religious claims as cognitively meaningless; verifiability principle.
Warranted Christian Belief 2000 argues belief in God is properly basic without inferential evidence.
Richard Swinburne's Existence of God 1979 uses principle of credulity; experiences are evidence absent defeaters.

concepts.def: Vienna Circle 1929 manifesto; A J Ayer popularised in 1936; statements meaningful if empirically verifiable or analytic.
Anthony Flew's 1950 University Discussion paper applied Karl Popper's principle; religious claims often die the death of a thousand qualifications.
Philosophical Investigations 1953; religious language is a distinct form of life with its own grammar; influence on D Z Phillips.
Aquinas's via analogiae (Summa Theologiae I q.13); attributes used analogically, not univocally or equivocally, of God.
Paul Tillich's Dynamics of Faith 1957; religious language symbolic, participating in what it symbolises, beyond literal description.
Apophatic via negativa (Pseudo-Dionysius c.500); cataphatic affirms positive attributes; both medieval Christian and Islamic kalam.

concepts.def: Epicurus c.300 BCE and J L Mackie's 1955 Evil and Omnipotence; God's attributes appear logically inconsistent with evil's existence.
William Rowe's 1979 fawn case argues quantity and distribution of evil makes God's existence improbable, not impossible.
Augustine of Hippo (354-430); evil is privatio boni; humanity inherited original sin via fall of Adam and Eve.
Irenaeus (c.130-202) and modernised by John Hick (Evil and the God of Love 1966); world as vale of soul-making.
Alvin Plantinga's God, Freedom and Evil 1974; God permits moral evil because creatures must be free to choose good.
Alfred North Whitehead 1929 and Charles Hartshorne; God persuades rather than coerces; evil arises from creatures' freedom.

Andrew Dickson White's Warfare of Science with Theology 1896; later challenged by Numbers and Lindberg as oversimplified.
Ian Barbour's Religion in an Age of Science 1990 distinguishes conflict, independence, dialogue and integration approaches.
Stephen Jay Gould's Non-Overlapping Magisteria in Rocks of Ages 1999; science explains facts, religion handles meaning and values.

Robert Bellah's 1967 essay on American civil religion; sacralised nationalism in presidential inaugural addresses.
Rule of religious authorities; Iran 1979 Islamic Republic under Khomeini codifies velayat-e faqih constitutional principle.
BJP and RSS in India (founded 1925) advance Hindutva; Buddhist nationalism in Myanmar (Ma Ba Tha 2014) and Sri Lanka.
French secular principle from 1905 Law on Separation of Church and State; 2004 headscarf ban in schools and 2010 burqa ban.

Karl Rahner's 1966 anonymous Christians; sincere non-Christians may be saved through Christ without explicit acknowledgement.
John Hick's An Interpretation of Religion 1989; great traditions are culturally conditioned responses to the Real.

George Lindbeck's The Nature of Doctrine 1984 cultural-linguistic model treats religions as incommensurable rule-governed practices.

Peter Berger's 1999 Desecularization of the World reversed his thesis; world is as furiously religious as ever, except Europe.
Robert Wuthnow's 1998 After Heaven described seekers; British Social Attitudes 2018 showed 52% no religion.
Rodney Stark and Roger Finke's Acts of Faith 2000; competition produces vitality; US disestablishment vs European monopolies.
Jose Casanova's Public Religions in the Modern World 1994; documented religion's continued public role in five case studies.
Richard Dawkins's God Delusion 2006, Sam Harris's End of Faith 2004, Christopher Hitchens's God Is Not Great 2007, Daniel Dennett.
